subject: chemistry
title: Word, balanced and ionic equations
key_idea: A chemical equation shows the reactants on the left and the products on the right. A balanced equation has the same number of each type of atom on both sides, because atoms are never made or destroyed. State symbols show the physical state of each substance.

blocks.text: A word equation names the substances in a reaction. This section covers how to write one and how to turn it into a symbol equation.

items.meaning: The substances at the start of a reaction. They go on the left of the arrow.
The substances made in a reaction. They go on the right of the arrow.
The symbols and small numbers that show which atoms are in a substance, such as H₂O or CO₂.

blocks.label: A word equation
where: Reactants are on the left. Products are on the right.

items: To write the symbol equation, replace each name with its formula.
Elements such as hydrogen, oxygen, nitrogen, chlorine and bromine are molecules of two atoms: H₂, O₂, N₂, Cl₂, Br₂.
The small number in a formula is part of the substance. It must **never** be changed to balance an equation.
Reactants go on the left, products on the right.
Get every formula right first. Balance second.
Never change the small numbers in a formula.

blocks.text: Atoms are not made or destroyed in a reaction. This section covers how to balance an equation by changing the big numbers in front of the formulae.

blocks.label: Methane burning in oxygen
where: The big numbers in front are the balancing numbers.
1 carbon, 4 hydrogen and 4 oxygen atoms on each side.

items.text: CH₄ + O₂ → CO₂ + H₂O. Check every formula before you start.
Left: 1 C, 4 H, 2 O. Right: 1 C, 2 H, 3 O.

items.lead: Balance one atom at a time.
items.text: Put 2 in front of H₂O to get 4 H. Now the right has 4 O.
Put 2 in front of O₂ on the left to get 4 O.
Left: 1 C, 4 H, 4 O. Right: 1 C, 4 H, 4 O. Balanced.

diagram.alt: Put the steps for balancing a symbol equation into the correct order.
steps: Write the correct formula for every reactant and product
Count the atoms of each element on both sides
Add a big number in front of a formula to balance one element
Recount all the atoms after each change
Check that every element is the same on both sides
diagram.prompt: Put the steps for balancing an equation in order

items: Change only the big numbers in front of formulae.
Balance one element at a time and recount.
A correct equation has the same atoms on both sides.

blocks.text: State symbols are written in brackets after each formula. They show the physical state of each substance.

blocks.label: With state symbols
where: Magnesium and magnesium oxide are solids at room temperature.

items: **Aqueous** means dissolved in water. It is not the same as liquid.
Water itself is (l), not (aq).
A precipitate, a solid that forms in a solution, is (s).
(s), (l), (g) and (aq) show the state of each substance.
(aq) means dissolved in water.
A precipitate is (s).

blocks.text: (Higher tier) An ionic equation shows only the particles that change in a reaction. Ions that are the same on both sides are left out.

items.meaning: An ion that is in the mixture but does not change. It is left out of the ionic equation.

items.text: Ba²⁺ + 2Cl⁻ + 2Na⁺ + SO₄²⁻ → BaSO₄(s) + 2Na⁺ + 2Cl⁻. Solids, liquids and gases stay as formulae.
2Na⁺ and 2Cl⁻ are on both sides, so they cancel.

diagram.alt: Sort each species into how it is written in an ionic equation.

items.text: An ion that is the same on both sides

diagram.prompt: How is each one written in an ionic equation?

items: The charges must balance as well as the atoms.
Zn(s) + Cu²⁺(aq) → Zn²⁺(aq) + Cu(s) has a total charge of 2+ on each side.
Only (aq) compounds are split into ions.
Cancel the spectator ions, which are the same on both sides.
The ionic equation balances in atoms and in charge.

checks.q: Balance this equation: Na₂O + H₂O → NaOH
What does the state symbol (aq) mean?
checks.a: Aqueous: the substance is dissolved in water.

checks.q: (Higher tier) Barium chloride solution reacts with sodium sulfate solution to form a precipitate. Write the ionic equation. Name the spectator ions.
checks.a: Ba²⁺(aq) + SO₄²⁻(aq) → BaSO₄(s). The spectator ions are Na⁺ and Cl⁻.

worked_example.question:
A student investigated the energy change of the reaction between zinc and copper sulfate solution.

Complete the ionic equation for the reaction between zinc and copper sulfate solution.

Include state symbols.

Zn(s) + Cu²⁺(aq) → _____ (   ) + _____ (   )
worked_example.tip: Zinc is more reactive, so it forms the ion in solution and copper is displaced as a solid. One mark can be given for the right species without the state symbols.

worked_example.question: Write the balanced equation for the complete combustion of octane, C₈H₁₈.
answer_points: C₈H₁₈ and O₂ on the left (1)
CO₂ and H₂O on the right (1)
worked_example.tip: Complete combustion makes carbon dioxide and water. Multiples, including halves, are allowed, and state symbols are ignored.

worked_example.question:
Sodium oxide, Na₂O, is a white solid.

Sodium oxide reacts with water.

An aqueous solution of sodium hydroxide is made.

Write the balanced symbol equation for this reaction, including state symbols.
answer_points: Correct formulae: Na₂O, H₂O and NaOH (1)
worked_example.tip: The state symbols mark is independent, so you can score it even if the balancing is wrong.
